glossary.Peritoneum: The thin membrane lining the abdominal cavity and covering the abdominal organs.
glossary.Abdominal distension: Swelling or bloating of the abdomen.
glossary.Peripheral oedema: Swelling of the legs and ankles from fluid in the tissues.
glossary.Superficial veins: Veins just under the skin; dilated abdominal veins suggest portal hypertension.
glossary.Chronic liver disease: Long-term liver damage lasting over six months, often leading to cirrhosis.
glossary.Ultrasound abdomen: Sound-wave imaging of the abdomen, very sensitive for free fluid.
glossary.LFTs: Liver function tests: ALT, AST, ALP, GGT, bilirubin and albumin.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes, a blood test of kidney function and salts.
glossary.INR: International normalised ratio, a clotting time that rises when the liver fails.
glossary.Ascitic fluid analysis: Lab tests on tapped ascitic fluid: cell count, albumin, culture and cytology.
glossary.Cell count: The number of white cells, especially neutrophils, in a fluid sample.
glossary.Neutrophils: The commonest white blood cells, which fight bacterial infection.
glossary.Albumin: The main blood protein, made by the liver, which holds fluid in vessels.
glossary.Right heart failure: Failure of the right ventricle, raising venous pressure and causing oedema and ascites.
glossary.TB: Tuberculosis, a mycobacterial infection that can cause peritoneal ascites.
glossary.Salt restriction: Limiting dietary sodium to reduce fluid retention.
glossary.Diuretic: A drug that increases urine output to remove excess fluid.
glossary.Titrated: Dose gradually adjusted up or down according to response.
glossary.Circulatory dysfunction: Failure to maintain adequate blood pressure and organ perfusion.
glossary.D-dimer: A breakdown product of clot; raised in DIC and thrombosis.
glossary.Fibrinogen: A clotting protein that is used up and falls in DIC.
glossary.IV antibiotics: Antibiotics given directly into a vein for serious infections.
glossary.Portosystemic shunt: A channel connecting the portal vein to the systemic veins, bypassing the liver.
glossary.Transjugular: Performed via a catheter passed through the jugular vein in the neck.
glossary.Sinusoids: The small leaky blood channels within the liver.
glossary.Splanchnic circulation: Blood supply to the gut, liver, spleen and pancreas.
glossary.Aldosterone: A hormone that makes the kidneys retain sodium and water.
glossary.Aldosterone antagonist: A drug such as spironolactone that blocks aldosterone's effect on the kidney.
glossary.Hypomotile: Moving less than normal; here, a sluggish gut.
glossary.Effective circulating volume: The part of the blood volume that actually fills the arteries and perfuses organs.
